questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: Rollover is the leading cause of truck-driver deaths in crashes involving heavy combinations. According to the CDL manual, what two practices most directly help prevent rollovers in a combination vehicle?

answers.text: Keep the cargo as close to the ground as possible, and drive slowly around turns
Use the trailer hand valve aggressively to keep the trailer in line
Lock the inter-axle differential in every left-hand curve
Reduce tire pressure by 20 percent in cold weather

explanations.a: The CDL manual states the two things that most help prevent rollover are keeping the cargo as close to the ground as possible and driving slowly around turns.
explanations.b: Aggressive trailer hand valve use can cause skids and is not the manual's rollover prevention.
explanations.c: Differential locks address traction, not rollover risk.
explanations.d: Reducing tire pressure does not address rollover and can create other handling problems.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: The CDL manual identifies a phenomenon where a quick steering input at the tractor causes a much larger, more violent motion at the rear trailer of a combination. What is this phenomenon called, and what does it cause?

answers.text: Off-tracking, which causes the trailer to follow a wider arc through turns
Rearward amplification, which produces the crack-the-whip effect that can flip the rear trailer in a quick lane change
Brake fade, which results from heat building up in the lining
Hydroplaning, which causes loss of traction at speeds as low as 30 mph

explanations.a: Off-tracking refers to the trailer's path during turns, not the lateral whip in lane changes.
explanations.b: The CDL manual describes rearward amplification as the cause of the crack-the-whip effect; in a quick lane change it can flip the rear trailer, with triples having a published rearward amplification of about 3.5.
explanations.c: Brake fade is a heat-related braking failure, unrelated to lateral lane-change dynamics.
explanations.d: Hydroplaning is a wet-pavement traction issue, not the lateral amplification phenomenon described.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: A driver bobtails a tractor (no trailer) back to the yard. The CDL manual gives a specific warning about how a bobtail tractor stops compared with a fully loaded combination. Which warning matches the manual?

answers.text: Bobtails always stop in less than half the distance of a loaded combination
Bobtails behave identically to a loaded combination under braking
Tests have shown bobtails can be very hard to stop smoothly, and they may take longer to stop than a tractor-semitrailer loaded to maximum gross weight
Bobtails may not be operated above 35 mph under any federal regulation

explanations.a: The manual specifically denies that bobtails always stop more quickly; tests show the opposite under many conditions.
explanations.b: Bobtails do not behave identically; the manual flags them as harder to stop smoothly.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states tests have shown bobtails can be very hard to stop smoothly and may take longer to stop than a tractor-semitrailer loaded to maximum gross weight.
explanations.d: There is no federal 35-mph speed limit specifically for bobtails.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: You see in the mirror that the trailer of your tractor-semitrailer is starting to swing out into a jackknife while braking on a slippery road. According to the CDL manual, what is the correct response?

answers.text: Apply the trailer hand valve harder to bring the trailer back in line
Apply the parking brakes immediately to stop both units
Steer sharply away from the trailer's swing direction while continuing to brake hard
Release the brakes to get traction back; do not use the trailer hand valve to straighten the rig, since brakes on the trailer wheels caused the skid

explanations.a: The manual specifically warns against using the trailer hand valve to straighten a jackknifing trailer; the brakes on the trailer wheels caused the skid in the first place.
explanations.b: Yanking the parking brakes worsens the lockup and the skid.
explanations.c: Sharp steering combined with hard braking deepens loss of control.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to release the brakes to regain traction; do not use the trailer hand valve to straighten the rig, because brakes on the trailer wheels caused the skid in the first place.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: An empty or lightly loaded tractor-trailer has different braking behavior than a fully loaded one. According to the CDL manual, what specific issue arises when the rig is empty?

answers.text: Stiff suspension springs and strong brakes give poor traction, and it is very easy to lock up the wheels
The empty trailer always stops in the shortest possible distance
The tractor's automatic transmission shifts up two gears to compensate
The trailer ABS deactivates because there is no weight on the wheels

explanations.a: The CDL manual states that when lightly loaded, the very stiff suspension springs and strong brakes give poor traction and make it very easy to lock up the wheels.
explanations.b: Empty rigs do not always stop in the shortest distance; the manual specifically warns about wheel-lock risk.
explanations.c: There is no automatic two-gear upshift triggered by an empty trailer.
explanations.d: ABS does not deactivate based on trailer load.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: On a routine straight-line stop on dry pavement, the CDL manual notes a counterintuitive comparison between empty and loaded large combination vehicles. Which statement matches the manual?

answers.text: Empty combinations stop in roughly half the distance of fully loaded ones
Large combination vehicles take longer to stop when they are empty than when they are fully loaded
Empty and loaded combinations always stop in identical distances
Federal regulation prohibits stopping-distance comparisons of empty rigs

explanations.a: The manual notes the opposite for combination vehicles; empty rigs typically take longer to stop.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states that large combination vehicles take longer to stop when they are empty than when they are fully loaded.
explanations.c: Empty and loaded stopping distances are not identical; the manual specifically distinguishes them.
explanations.d: There is no federal prohibition on stopping-distance comparisons of empty rigs.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: The CDL manual cites a striking comparison between fully loaded and empty rigs in rollover crashes. About how much more likely are fully loaded rigs to roll over in a crash than empty ones?

answers.text: About 2 times more likely
About 5 times more likely
About 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs
About 50 times more likely

explanations.a: 2 times underestimates the figure cited in the manual.
explanations.b: 5 times still underestimates the published figure.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states that fully loaded rigs are 10 times more likely to roll over in a crash than empty rigs.
explanations.d: 50 times overstates the manual's published figure.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: The CDL manual cites a sobering statistic about how truck-driver deaths in crashes are distributed between rollover events and other crash types. Which statement matches the manual's data?

answers.text: About 5 percent of truck driver deaths are from rollovers
About 20 percent of truck driver deaths are from rollovers
Rollovers account for under one third of truck driver deaths in crashes
More than half of truck driver deaths in crashes are the result of truck rollovers

explanations.a: 5 percent is well below the manual's figure for rollover-related driver deaths.
explanations.b: 20 percent still understates the manual's figure.
explanations.c: The published figure is greater than one-third; rollovers account for the majority.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states more than half of truck driver deaths in crashes are the result of truck rollovers.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: The CDL manual uses a specific term to describe how the rear wheels of a combination vehicle follow a different path than the front wheels through a turn. Which definition matches the manual?

answers.text: Off-tracking, also called cheating, where the rear wheels follow a tighter path inside the front wheels' path through a corner
Crab steering, where each axle pivots independently
Toe-in, where the front wheels point toward the centerline
Camber roll, where the rear axle leans outward through curves

explanations.a: The CDL manual defines off-tracking, also called cheating, as the phenomenon where the rear wheels follow a different (tighter) path than the front wheels through a turn.
explanations.b: Crab steering describes deliberate independent steering, not the natural rear-axle behavior in a turn.
explanations.c: Toe-in is a wheel-alignment angle, not the path-following behavior in a turn.
explanations.d: Camber roll is not the manual's term for the rear-axle path through a corner.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: For a triple-trailer combination, the CDL manual makes a specific point about which trailer's wheels off-track the most through a corner. Which statement matches the manual?

answers.text: The first trailer's wheels off-track the most
The rear wheels of the last trailer off-track the most
All trailers off-track equally because they share the same kingpin geometry
None of the trailer wheels off-track because the dolly absorbs all of the path difference

explanations.a: The first trailer's wheels off-track somewhat, but not as much as the last trailer's wheels.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states that if there is more than one trailer, the rear wheels of the last trailer off-track the most.
explanations.c: The trailers do not off-track equally; the path-difference accumulates through the train.
explanations.d: Dollies do not absorb path differences; they pass them along to the next trailer.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: At a tight intersection, a combination vehicle cannot make a right turn without entering another lane. According to the CDL manual, what is the correct technique?

answers.text: Stop the truck in the intersection and back up after waiting for traffic to clear
Swing wide to the left before starting the turn so the trailer has plenty of room
Turn wide as you complete the turn while keeping the rear of the vehicle close to the curb
Cross into oncoming traffic to give the trailer the maximum possible arc

explanations.a: Backing in an intersection is hazardous and not the manual's prescribed method.
explanations.b: The manual specifically warns against swinging wide to the left first because following drivers may try to pass on the right.
explanations.c: The CDL manual instructs drivers to turn wide as they complete the turn while keeping the rear of the vehicle close to the curb, to prevent other drivers from passing on the right.
explanations.d: Crossing into oncoming traffic creates a head-on hazard and is not the manual's recommended technique.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: The CDL manual specifically warns against one common but dangerous turn-setup mistake among CMV drivers. Which mistake does the manual call out, and why is it dangerous?

answers.text: Using both mirrors before initiating the turn, which can cause delayed steering input
Activating the turn signal too early, which gives traffic too much time to adjust
Using the trailer hand valve to slow into the turn, which can cause the trailer to swing
Swinging wide to the left as you start a right turn, because following drivers may think you are turning left and try to pass you on the right

explanations.a: Using both mirrors is good practice; the manual encourages it.
explanations.b: The manual encourages signaling well in advance; it is not a dangerous mistake.
explanations.c: While the trailer hand valve should not be used in driving, it is not the specific turn-setup mistake the manual flags.
explanations.d: The CDL manual warns drivers not to swing wide to the left as they start a right turn, because a following driver may think the truck is turning left and try to pass on the right, causing a crash as the truck completes the turn.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: When a CMV driver must back along a curved path with a trailer, the CDL manual gives a clear preference for one direction over the other. Which preference matches the manual?

answers.text: Back to the driver's side so you can see the trailer through the side window
Back to the right side so the trailer can use the curb as a guide
Back straight only; never back along a curved path under any circumstance
Back along whichever side has the larger mirror, regardless of which side that is

explanations.a: The CDL manual instructs drivers to back to the driver's side along curved paths so they can see the trailer through the side window.
explanations.b: Backing to the right (passenger side) is blind backing and is not the manual's preferred method.
explanations.c: Backing along a curved path is sometimes necessary; the manual gives guidance for it.
explanations.d: The driver's-side preference is about visibility from the cab, not mirror size.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: Backing a trailer behaves differently than backing a single straight truck. According to the CDL manual, what is the key steering rule when starting to back a trailer in a chosen direction?

answers.text: Turn the steering wheel in the same direction as the desired trailer movement
Turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of the desired trailer movement, then turn it back the other way once the trailer starts to follow
Hold the steering wheel still and shift weight in the cab to steer the trailer
Tap the trailer hand valve to nudge the trailer in the desired direction

explanations.a: Turning in the same direction as the desired trailer movement is the rule for straight trucks, not trailers.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states that when backing a trailer, the driver turns the steering wheel in the opposite direction; once the trailer starts to turn, the driver must turn the wheel the other way to follow the trailer.
explanations.c: Cab weight shifts do not steer trailers.
explanations.d: The trailer hand valve operates trailer brakes, not steering.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: Before beginning to back a trailer into a tight spot, the CDL manual gives a specific pre-backing routine. Which step does the manual prescribe?

answers.text: Apply the parking brake and exit the cab to lock the doors
Disconnect the trailer service line and rely on the parking brake during backing
Look at your line of travel before you begin; get out and walk around the vehicle, checking clearance to the sides and overhead
Set the trailer hand valve to half-open to slow the trailer reactively

explanations.a: Locking doors before backing is not the manual's pre-backing step.
explanations.b: Disconnecting the service line during backing is not in the manual's procedure.
explanations.c: The CDL manual instructs drivers to look at their line of travel before they begin, get out and walk around the vehicle, and check clearance to the sides and overhead.
explanations.d: The trailer hand valve is not used in driving operations including backing.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: During a difficult backing maneuver, the trailer begins drifting off the intended line. According to the CDL manual, what corrective action does the manual recommend if the drift cannot be fixed in reverse alone?

answers.text: Continue backing until the trailer aligns with the driver's seat angle
Apply the parking brake and call dispatch for assistance
Use the trailer hand valve to lock the trailer in place and force it to follow
Make pull-ups to re-position the vehicle as needed when backing a trailer

explanations.a: Continuing to back without pull-ups deepens drift; the manual prescribes pull-ups instead.
explanations.b: Calling dispatch is not the immediate technique; pull-ups are.
explanations.c: Using the trailer hand valve at any time except testing is contrary to the manual's guidance.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to make pull-ups (pull forward, then back again) to re-position the vehicle as needed when backing a trailer.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: The first step of the CDL manual's coupling procedure for a tractor-semitrailer is to inspect the fifth wheel. Which set of conditions does the manual say to verify before backing under the trailer?

answers.text: Wheel tilted down toward the rear of the tractor, jaws open, and safety unlocking handle in the automatic lock position
Wheel tilted down toward the front of the tractor with jaws closed and locked
Fifth wheel removed entirely from the tractor for inspection
Fifth wheel pre-greased only after the trailer is connected

explanations.a: The CDL manual instructs drivers to confirm the fifth wheel is tilted down toward the rear of the tractor, the jaws are open, and the safety unlocking handle is in the automatic lock position before backing under the trailer.
explanations.b: Tilting toward the front and jaws closed are exactly the conditions that prevent coupling.
explanations.c: The fifth wheel is not removed for inspection; it stays on the tractor.
explanations.d: The manual instructs that the fifth wheel plate must be greased before coupling, not after.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: After lining up the tractor with the trailer for coupling, the CDL manual prescribes a specific check on trailer height before backing under. Which check matches the manual?

answers.text: The trailer should be raised so it is well above the fifth wheel for clearance
The trailer should be low enough that it is raised slightly by the tractor when the tractor backs under it; raise or lower the trailer as needed
The trailer height does not matter as long as the kingpin is in the correct position
The trailer must be exactly level with the fifth wheel, with no clearance and no contact

explanations.a: A trailer set well above the fifth wheel will not couple correctly.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states the trailer should be low enough that it is raised slightly by the tractor when the tractor backs under it; the driver must raise or lower the trailer as needed.
explanations.c: Trailer height matters; the manual specifically requires the slight-lift condition.
explanations.d: Exactly level with no clearance does not produce the slight-lift condition the manual requires.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: After verifying trailer height and connecting initial setup steps, the CDL manual gives a precise instruction for the first phase of backing during coupling. Which instruction matches the manual?

answers.text: Back at moderate speed to drive the kingpin firmly into the locking jaws
Back until the trailer brakes contact the rear of the tractor frame
Back slowly until the fifth wheel just touches the trailer; do not hit the trailer
Reverse with one wheel up on a curb to align the fifth wheel automatically

explanations.a: Moderate-speed backing risks damage and is not the manual's procedure.
explanations.b: Trailer brakes never contact the tractor frame; that is not part of any coupling step.
explanations.c: The CDL manual instructs drivers to back slowly until the fifth wheel just touches the trailer, and not to hit the trailer.
explanations.d: Curb-based alignment is not the manual's coupling method.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: After backing the tractor under the trailer until the kingpin is locked, the CDL manual prescribes a specific test to verify the connection is secure before continuing. Which test matches the manual?

answers.text: Pull forward at full throttle while the trailer brakes are released
Slam the brakes hard with the parking brake released to check kingpin retention
Push the trailer rearward with the bumper to confirm it does not move
Raise the trailer landing gear slightly off the ground, then pull the tractor gently forward while the trailer brakes are still locked, to check that the trailer is locked onto the tractor

explanations.a: Pulling forward at full throttle is dangerous and is not the test described in the manual.
explanations.b: Slamming the brakes with the parking brake released is not the manual's connection test.
explanations.c: Pushing the trailer rearward with the bumper is not in the manual's coupling procedure.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to raise the trailer landing gear slightly off the ground, then pull the tractor gently forward while the trailer brakes are still locked, to check that the trailer is locked onto the tractor.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: After confirming the connection is secure, the CDL manual gives a specific instruction about the landing gear before driving away. Which instruction matches the manual?

answers.text: Raise the landing gear all the way up; never drive with landing gear only part way up, since it may catch on railroad tracks or other things
Leave the landing gear extended halfway to provide a safety prop in case of fifth wheel failure
Raise the landing gear only until it just lifts off the pavement, no further
Remove the landing gear entirely before driving

explanations.a: The CDL manual instructs drivers to raise the landing gear all the way up and never to drive with landing gear only part way up because it may catch on railroad tracks or other things.
explanations.b: A halfway position creates exactly the catch hazard the manual warns against.
explanations.c: Raising only until lift-off leaves the gear extended low enough to catch obstacles.
explanations.d: Landing gear is part of the trailer; it is not removed before driving.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.keyword: electrical cord and air line check
questions.text: After raising the landing gear, the CDL manual specifies one more electrical and pneumatic step before driving. Which step matches the manual?

answers.text: Disconnect the trailer ABS power and reconnect it after the trip
Plug the electrical cord into the trailer, fasten the safety catch, and check both air-lines and the electrical line for signs of damage and that they will not hit any moving parts
Turn off the trailer ABS so it will not interfere with the tractor system
Cover the glad hands with grease to prevent moisture intrusion

explanations.a: Disconnecting trailer ABS power is not part of the manual's coupling procedure.
explanations.b: The CDL manual instructs drivers to plug the electrical cord into the trailer and fasten the safety catch, then check both air-lines and the electrical line for damage and that they will not hit any moving parts of the vehicle.
explanations.c: Turning off trailer ABS is not in the manual's procedure.
explanations.d: Glad hand seals are not greased; they are cleaned and pressed together at a 90-degree angle.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.keyword: no space upper lower fifth wheel
questions.text: During the post-coupling inspection, the CDL manual identifies a specific space-related defect that indicates a dangerous coupling. Which observation should trigger the driver to refuse to drive the unit?

answers.text: A small bead of grease visible at the edge of the fifth wheel plate
Slight discoloration of the kingpin from heat
Visible space between the upper and lower fifth wheel — if there is space, the kingpin may be on top of the closed jaws and the trailer would come loose very easily
Even tire wear visible across all trailer tires

explanations.a: Visible grease is normal; the manual instructs drivers to keep the fifth wheel plate greased.
explanations.b: Heat discoloration of the kingpin is not the specific defect the manual identifies.
explanations.c: The CDL manual states there must be no visible space between the upper and lower fifth wheel after coupling; if there is space, the kingpin may be on top of the closed jaws and the trailer would come loose very easily.
explanations.d: Even tire wear is good news, not a defect.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: The CDL manual gives a precise inspection criterion for the fifth wheel locking jaws after coupling. Which criterion matches the manual?

answers.text: The jaws must be partially open around the kingpin to allow trailer movement
The jaws must clamp around the head of the kingpin only
The jaws must be left half-engaged to permit easy uncoupling later
The locking jaws must be closed around the shank of the kingpin, not the head

explanations.a: Partially open jaws indicate an unsafe coupling.
explanations.b: Clamping only the head of the kingpin is exactly the failure mode the manual warns about.
explanations.c: Half-engaged jaws are unsafe and not the manual's inspection criterion.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states the locking jaws must be around the shank, not the head, of the kingpin.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: The CDL manual lays out a step-by-step uncoupling procedure starting with positioning the rig. Which positioning instructions match the manual's first step?

answers.text: Make sure the surface of the parking area can support the weight of the trailer, and have the tractor lined up with the trailer to avoid damaging landing gear
Park the rig on a steep crowned surface to prevent the trailer from rolling
Park with the tractor at a 45-degree angle to the trailer to ease unlatching
Park on grass or gravel to absorb shock when the landing gear lowers

explanations.a: The CDL manual instructs drivers to make sure the surface of the parking area can support the weight of the trailer and to have the tractor lined up with the trailer to avoid damaging the landing gear when the tractor pulls out.
explanations.b: A steep crowned surface is unsafe for uncoupling.
explanations.c: A 45-degree angle would damage the landing gear when the tractor pulls forward.
explanations.d: Soft surfaces such as gravel can let the landing gear sink and are not the manual's preferred parking surface.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: During uncoupling, the CDL manual prescribes a wheel-chocking step under specific conditions. Which condition matches the manual?

answers.text: Chock the trailer wheels only when the trailer is empty and on a downgrade
Chock the trailer wheels if the trailer doesn't have spring brakes or if you're not sure, since air could leak out of the trailer air tank and release the emergency brakes
Chock the trailer wheels only after the tractor is fully clear and out of sight
Chocking is required only for triples, never for tractor-semitrailers

explanations.a: The empty/downgrade condition is not the manual's chocking trigger.
explanations.b: The CDL manual instructs drivers to chock the trailer wheels if the trailer does not have spring brakes or if the driver is unsure, because air could leak out of the trailer air tank and release the emergency brakes, allowing the trailer to move.
explanations.c: Chocking after the tractor leaves is too late if the trailer rolls.
explanations.d: Chocking applies to any trailer without spring brakes, not only triples.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: When lowering the landing gear during uncoupling, the CDL manual gives a different instruction depending on whether the trailer is loaded or empty. Which instruction matches the manual for a loaded trailer?

answers.text: Lower the landing gear until it just clears the ground, with no contact
Lower the landing gear and lift the trailer fully off the fifth wheel before unlatching
After the landing gear makes firm contact with the ground, turn the crank in low gear a few extra turns to lift some weight off the tractor; do not lift the trailer off the fifth wheel
Skip the landing gear entirely and rely on stacked wood blocks under the trailer nose

explanations.a: Just clearing the ground does not transfer enough weight off the tractor for a loaded trailer.
explanations.b: Lifting the trailer fully off the fifth wheel can damage components and is not the manual's instruction.
explanations.c: The CDL manual instructs drivers that for a loaded trailer, after the landing gear makes firm contact with the ground, the driver should turn the crank in low gear a few extra turns to lift some weight off the tractor, but not lift the trailer off the fifth wheel.
explanations.d: Wood blocks are not a substitute for the trailer's landing gear.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: After unlocking the fifth wheel during uncoupling, the CDL manual prescribes a specific intermediate position for the tractor before fully driving away. Which position matches the manual?

answers.text: Pull the tractor completely clear of the trailer immediately, then return for inspection
Pull forward only until the air-line glad hands disconnect themselves
Pull forward until the kingpin is centered between the front and rear axles of the tractor

Pull the tractor forward until the fifth wheel comes out from under the trailer, but stop with the tractor frame still under the trailer to prevent the trailer from falling to the ground if the landing gear should collapse or sink

explanations.a: Pulling fully clear immediately leaves no safety net if the landing gear collapses.
explanations.b: Glad hands do not disconnect themselves during the pull-forward phase.
explanations.c: Centering the kingpin between tractor axles is not the manual's intermediate position.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to pull the tractor forward until the fifth wheel comes out from under the trailer, but to stop with the tractor frame still under the trailer to prevent the trailer from falling to the ground if the landing gear should collapse or sink.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: For a combination vehicle, the CDL manual instructs drivers to use the same seven-step inspection method as for a single vehicle, with additional items added in the appropriate steps. Which statement best summarizes the manual's instruction?

answers.text: Use the seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2 to inspect the combination vehicle, with additional combination-specific items added in their proper steps
Skip the seven-step procedure entirely and inspect only the coupling system
Use a separate eleven-step procedure that has nothing in common with the single-vehicle method
Have a mechanic perform all inspections; drivers do not inspect combination vehicles

explanations.a: The CDL manual instructs drivers to use the seven-step inspection procedure described in Section 2 to inspect a combination vehicle, with additional combination-specific items added in their proper steps.
explanations.b: Skipping the seven-step procedure is contrary to the manual.
explanations.c: There is no separate eleven-step procedure replacing the standard seven steps.
explanations.d: Drivers are required to perform pre-trip inspections themselves; mechanics do not substitute.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: During the walk-around portion of a combination-vehicle inspection, the CDL manual lists specific items to verify on the lower fifth wheel. Which item is among them?

answers.text: Verify the fifth wheel rotates freely 360 degrees on its own
Verify the fifth wheel is securely mounted to the frame, with no missing or damaged parts and enough grease
Verify the fifth wheel is painted matte black for visibility
Verify the fifth wheel is removable by hand for cleaning

explanations.a: The fifth wheel does not rotate freely 360 degrees; it pivots only over a limited angular range.
explanations.b: The CDL manual lists checks for the lower fifth wheel including secure mounting to the frame, no missing or damaged parts, enough grease, and no visible space between upper and lower fifth wheel.
explanations.c: There is no paint-color requirement on the fifth wheel.
explanations.d: The fifth wheel is bolted to the frame and is not hand-removable for cleaning.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: When inspecting the upper fifth wheel and the kingpin area, the CDL manual gives several specific checks. Which set matches the manual?

answers.text: Verify the kingpin spins freely and the glide plate is smooth
Verify the kingpin is removable for off-truck inspection
Verify the glide plate is securely mounted to the trailer frame and the kingpin is not damaged
Verify the kingpin shows visible heat-bluing for proper hardening

explanations.a: A freely spinning kingpin is a defect, not a normal condition.
explanations.b: The kingpin is fixed to the trailer; it is not removed for off-truck inspection.
explanations.c: The CDL manual lists checks for the upper fifth wheel including that the glide plate is securely mounted to the trailer frame and the kingpin is not damaged.
explanations.d: Heat bluing on a kingpin would indicate an overheating problem, not normal condition.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: On a tractor with a sliding fifth wheel, the CDL manual lists specific items to verify during the walk-around. Which set matches the manual's required checks?

answers.text: Slide unlocked, all rollers exposed, and the fifth wheel free to move under throttle
Slide chassis painted yellow with at least three reflective markers
Slide grease purged and dry to prevent contamination
Slide not damaged or parts missing, properly greased, all locking pins present and locked in place, and if air-powered, no air leaks

explanations.a: An unlocked slide free to move under throttle is exactly the unsafe condition the manual warns against.
explanations.b: Yellow paint and reflective markers are not part of the manual's slide inspection.
explanations.c: Grease must be present, not purged.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to verify the sliding fifth wheel slide is not damaged or parts missing, properly greased, all locking pins present and locked in place, and if air powered, no air leaks.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: During the combination-vehicle walk-around, the CDL manual specifies inspection criteria for the air-lines and electrical lines between tractor and trailer. Which criteria match the manual?

answers.text: Air-lines properly connected to glad hands, no air leaks, properly secured with enough slack for turns; all lines free from damage
Air-lines pulled taut between tractor and trailer to minimize whipping
Air-lines disconnected during inspection and reconnected only at trip start
Air-lines spliced together with red electrical tape if any abrasion is found

explanations.a: The CDL manual instructs drivers to check that air-lines are properly connected to glad hands, leak-free, and properly secured with enough slack for turns, with all lines free from damage.
explanations.b: Pulling lines taut prevents safe turning and is the opposite of the manual's instruction.
explanations.c: Disconnecting air-lines for the walk-around is not the manual's procedure.
explanations.d: Tape splices on damaged air-lines are not authorized by the manual; damaged lines must be repaired or replaced.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.keyword: test air flows to all trailers
questions.text: On a combination with one or more trailers, the CDL manual prescribes a test to verify air flows all the way through the system. Which procedure matches the manual?

answers.text: Disconnect each glad hand in turn and listen for air

With the parking brake set or wheels chocked and air pressure normal, push in the trailer air supply knob and use the trailer hand brake; go to the rear of the rig and open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer to listen for escaping air, then close it; open the service line shut-off valve to verify service pressure goes through, then close it
Drive the rig at 5 mph while pumping the brake pedal and listen for air leaks
Disconnect the trailer ABS module and check the diagnostic codes

explanations.a: Disconnecting glad hands in sequence is not the manual's procedure for verifying air flow to all trailers.
explanations.b: The CDL manual instructs drivers to use the parking brake or chocks, push in the trailer air supply knob, and use the trailer hand brake; then at the rear of the rig, open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer to confirm escaping air, close it, and open the service line valve to confirm service pressure flow.
explanations.c: Driving while pumping the brakes is not the static test the manual describes.
explanations.d: Diagnostic codes are not the manual's prescribed verification of air flow.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: During the combination-vehicle brake check, the CDL manual prescribes a test to verify the tractor protection valve. Which procedure matches the manual?

answers.text: Disconnect the trailer service line at the glad hand and watch the gauge
Apply the trailer hand valve at full force for one minute

Charge the trailer air-brake system, shut the engine off, and step on and off the brake pedal several times to reduce air pressure; the trailer air supply control should pop out (or go from 'normal' to 'emergency') when air pressure falls into the manufacturer-specified range, usually 20 to 45 psi
Drive at 25 mph and apply the parking brake to depressurize both circuits

explanations.a: Disconnecting at the glad hand is unsafe and is not the manual's procedure for this test.
explanations.b: Holding the trailer hand valve at full force is not the manual's procedure.
explanations.c: The CDL manual instructs drivers to charge the trailer air-brake system, shut the engine off, and step on and off the brake pedal to reduce air pressure; the trailer air supply control should pop out when air pressure falls into the manufacturer-specified range, usually 20 to 45 psi.
explanations.d: Yanking the parking brake at speed is dangerous and not the test.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.text: To verify trailer service brakes are connected and working during the combination-vehicle brake check, the CDL manual prescribes a specific procedure with the trailer hand control. Which procedure matches the manual?

answers.text: Disconnect the trailer service line and apply the trailer hand brake at full force
Apply the foot pedal only and verify air pressure drops on the gauge
Engage the parking brake, raise the trailer landing gear, and rock the rig forward and backward

Wait for normal air pressure, release the parking brakes, move the vehicle forward slowly, and apply trailer brakes with the hand control if so equipped; the driver should feel the brakes come on, confirming the trailer brakes are connected and working

explanations.a: Disconnecting the service line is not the procedure described in the manual.
explanations.b: Applying only the foot pedal does not isolate the trailer brakes for the connection test.
explanations.c: Engaging the parking brake and rocking the rig is not the manual's procedure.
explanations.d: The CDL manual instructs drivers to wait for normal air pressure, release the parking brakes, move the vehicle forward slowly, and apply the trailer brakes with the hand control; feeling the brakes come on confirms they are connected and working.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.objective: 5.5 Trailer brake hand valve, trailer air supply, fifth wheel, kingpin, locking jaws, glad hands, dolly couplers
questions.keyword: trailer hand valve only for testing
questions.text: The trailer hand valve, sometimes called the trolley valve or Johnson bar, has a specific intended use described in the CDL manual. Which use matches the manual?

answers.text: It should be used only to test the trailer brakes; it should not be used in driving because of the danger of making the trailer skid
It should be used as the primary brake control during normal driving
It should be used as the parking brake whenever the rig is stopped
It should be used to gradually apply the spring brakes during downgrades

explanations.a: The CDL manual states the trailer hand valve should be used only to test the trailer brakes and should not be used in driving because of the danger of making the trailer skid.
explanations.b: Using the hand valve as primary control during driving causes trailer skids and jackknifes.
explanations.c: The hand valve is not a parking brake; the manual specifically warns the air can leak away.
explanations.d: Spring-brake gradual application is via the modulating control valve, not the trailer hand valve.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.objective: 5.5 Trailer brake hand valve, trailer air supply, fifth wheel, kingpin, locking jaws, glad hands, dolly couplers
questions.text: The tractor protection valve has a specific automatic behavior at low air pressure. According to the CDL manual, when does the tractor protection valve automatically close?

answers.text: When the engine is started
When air pressure drops into the range of 20 to 45 psi, stopping any air from going out of the tractor and letting the air out of the trailer emergency line
When the parking brake control is engaged on the trailer only
When the cab door is opened with the engine running

explanations.a: The valve does not close at engine start; it closes on low air pressure.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states the tractor protection valve closes automatically when air pressure is low, in the range of 20 to 45 psi, stopping any air from going out of the tractor and letting the air out of the trailer emergency line.
explanations.c: Engaging the trailer parking brake is not the trigger for tractor protection valve closure.
explanations.d: Cab door state does not affect the tractor protection valve.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.objective: 5.5 Trailer brake hand valve, trailer air supply, fifth wheel, kingpin, locking jaws, glad hands, dolly couplers
questions.text: Every combination vehicle has two air-lines running between each unit. According to the CDL manual, what is the difference between the service line and the emergency line?

answers.text: The service line carries hydraulic fluid; the emergency line carries air
Both lines carry the same air supply at the same pressure

The service line (also called control or signal line) carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake; the emergency line (also called supply line) supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls emergency brakes — loss of pressure causes the emergency brakes to come on
The service line is for the tractor brakes only; the emergency line is for the trailer parking brake only

explanations.a: Both lines carry compressed air, not hydraulic fluid.
explanations.b: The two lines serve different functions and operate at different pressures.
explanations.c: The CDL manual explains that the service line carries air controlled by the foot brake or trailer hand brake, with pressure varying based on pedal pressure; the emergency line supplies air to the trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes, with loss of pressure causing the emergency brakes to come on.
explanations.d: This split mischaracterizes both lines; both lines extend to the trailer and serve trailer-specific roles.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.objective: 5.5 Trailer brake hand valve, trailer air supply, fifth wheel, kingpin, locking jaws, glad hands, dolly couplers
questions.text: The CDL manual identifies two distinct purposes that the emergency air-line serves on a combination vehicle. Which pair of purposes matches the manual?

answers.text: It carries hydraulic pressure to the trailer brakes and signals trailer turn signals
It cools the trailer air compressor and powers cabin heat
It applies the parking brake and disengages the locking jaws
It supplies air to the trailer air tanks, and it controls the emergency brakes — a loss of pressure causes the trailer emergency brakes to come on

explanations.a: The line is pneumatic, not hydraulic, and is unrelated to turn signals.
explanations.b: The trailer compressor and cabin heat are not connected to the emergency line.
explanations.c: The emergency line does not engage parking brakes or disengage locking jaws.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states the emergency line has two purposes: it supplies air to the trailer air tanks, and it controls the emergency brakes; loss of pressure in the emergency line causes the trailer emergency brakes to come on.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.objective: 5.5 Trailer brake hand valve, trailer air supply, fifth wheel, kingpin, locking jaws, glad hands, dolly couplers
questions.text: Glad hands are the coupling devices that connect the air-lines from the tractor or truck to the trailer. According to the CDL manual, what is the proper procedure for connecting glad hands?

answers.text: Clean the couplers and rubber seals before connecting; press the two seals together with the couplers at a 90-degree angle to each other; a turn of the glad hand attached to the hose joins and locks the couplers
Apply heavy grease to the rubber seals before mating; align the couplers parallel and pull straight to lock
Connect the couplers wet from a steam cleaner so debris flushes out before locking
Strike the couplers with a heavy mallet to seat the seals

explanations.a: The CDL manual instructs drivers to clean the couplers and rubber seals before connecting, press the two seals together with the couplers at a 90-degree angle to each other, and turn the glad hand attached to the hose to join and lock the couplers.
explanations.b: Heavy grease damages rubber seals; the manual specifies cleaning, not greasing.
explanations.c: Wetting the seals from a steam cleaner is not the manual's connection method.
explanations.d: Striking with a mallet damages glad hands and seals.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.objective: 5.5 Trailer brake hand valve, trailer air supply, fifth wheel, kingpin, locking jaws, glad hands, dolly couplers
questions.text: Shut-off valves (cut-out cocks) are installed in the service and supply air-lines at the back of trailers used to tow other trailers. According to the CDL manual, what is the correct configuration of these valves on a doubles or triples combination?

answers.text: All shut-off valves should be in the closed position to isolate each trailer's brakes
All shut-off valves should be in the open position except the ones at the back of the last trailer, which must be closed
All shut-off valves should be in the closed position except the ones at the back of the lead trailer, which must be open
Shut-off valves are decorative only and the position does not matter

explanations.a: Closing all valves prevents air flow to the trailer brakes and is unsafe.
explanations.b: The CDL manual states all shut-off valves must be in the open position except the ones at the back of the last trailer, which must be closed.
explanations.c: Reversing this configuration prevents air flow to the rear trailers.
explanations.d: The valves are functional and their position is critical to braking on every trailer.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.objective: 5.5 Trailer brake hand valve, trailer air supply, fifth wheel, kingpin, locking jaws, glad hands, dolly couplers
questions.text: On newer combination vehicles, the dashboard control that operates the tractor protection valve has a specific shape and color. According to the CDL manual, which description matches the trailer air supply control on newer vehicles?

answers.text: A green four-sided knob labeled 'air'
A blue round push-button labeled 'air'
A red eight-sided knob; push it in to supply the trailer with air, pull it out to shut the air off and apply the trailer emergency brakes
A yellow diamond knob identical to the parking brake control

explanations.a: The trailer air supply is not a green four-sided knob.
explanations.b: It is not a blue round push-button.
explanations.c: The CDL manual describes the trailer air supply control on newer vehicles as a red eight-sided knob; the driver pushes it in to supply the trailer with air and pulls it out to shut the air off and apply the trailer emergency brakes.
explanations.d: The yellow diamond knob is the parking brake control, which is distinct from the red trailer air supply.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.objective: 5.5 Trailer brake hand valve, trailer air supply, fifth wheel, kingpin, locking jaws, glad hands, dolly couplers
questions.text: To help drivers avoid mismatched glad hand connections during coupling, the CDL manual notes a common color-coding convention. Which mapping matches the manual?

answers.text: Green for the service line and yellow for the emergency line
Black for the service line and white for the emergency line
Orange for the service line and purple for the emergency line
Blue is used for the service lines and red for the emergency (supply) lines

explanations.a: Green and yellow are not the manual's coding convention.
explanations.b: Black and white are not the manual's coding convention.
explanations.c: Orange and purple are not the manual's coding convention.
explanations.d: The CDL manual states that to help avoid mistakes, blue is used for the service lines and red for the emergency (supply) lines, and metal tags are sometimes attached to the lines stamped 'service' and 'emergency'.

questions.name: Combination Vehicles
questions.objective: 5.5 Trailer brake hand valve, trailer air supply, fifth wheel, kingpin, locking jaws, glad hands, dolly couplers
questions.text: Each trailer and converter dolly has one or more air tanks. According to the CDL manual, what is the proper drainage practice for these trailer air tanks?

answers.text: Drain each tank every day; even if the tanks have automatic drains, open the drains to make sure
Never drain the tanks because the manufacturer pre-charges them at the factory
Drain the tanks only after a tire failure
Drain the tanks only after a steep downgrade

explanations.a: The CDL manual instructs drivers to drain each trailer air tank every day; even if the tanks have automatic drains, the driver should still open the drains to make sure.
explanations.b: Tanks are not pre-charged at the factory and require daily attention.
explanations.c: Tire failure is not the trigger for tank draining.
explanations.d: Downgrade descent is not the trigger for tank draining.
